status: User approved for initial use; subject to later SLP review

rows.lookListen: Listen to the beginning of your story. Who do you hear about?
rows.think: Who is your story mostly about?
rows.clue: If it’s hard to tell who the story is about, name the main character near the beginning.
rows.moreHelp: Ask the student to identify the main character in their own story. Contrast an introduction with an action from later in the story, then have the student place their introduction where the listener needs it.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen for information about where or when the story begins.
rows.think: Where does this part happen?
rows.clue: If the place matters, add it where this part begins. If the time matters more, tell when it happens.
rows.moreHelp: Identify a relevant place or time already established in the student’s story. Help the student decide whether the listener needs it before the next event; do not add a new setting.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Listen to the beginning. Can your listener tell what the character is trying to do?
rows.think: What was the character trying to do, and what got in the way?
rows.clue: Put the problem where the listener needs it. If Maya is already searching, tell us what she lost.
rows.moreHelp: Separate the problem from a later response or attempt using the student’s own content. Ask which part creates the difficulty and where the listener needs to hear it.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen for a feeling that matters to this part of your story.
rows.think: Where would it help to tell how the character feels?
rows.clue: If the feeling helps explain this part, put it near the moment it belongs to.
rows.moreHelp: Check whether the student intends a feeling here. If so, help locate it near the event it relates to; accept a feeling conveyed through action or dialogue when that serves the target.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen for what the character intends or decides to do.
rows.think: What did the character plan to do?
rows.clue: If your story has a plan, tell it where the listener needs it. Then tell what the character actually did.
rows.moreHelp: Use the student’s own plan and action to distinguish intention from performance. If the story has no stated plan, decide whether adding one serves the narrative target; do not invent it.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen for what the character actually does.
rows.think: What did the character actually do?
rows.clue: Tell the action where it belongs in the story. If there were two tries, put them where the listener can follow them.
rows.moreHelp: Identify the student’s intended action, then place it relative to the problem and any plan. If more than one attempt matters, organize those attempts without requiring a successful outcome.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen for the outcome at the end of your story.
rows.think: How did things turn out?
rows.clue: Tell what changed or what was still a problem at the end.
rows.sentenceHelp: In the end, ___. / The problem was still ___.
rows.moreHelp: Compare the ending with the original problem using the student’s content. Help the student explain the actual outcome; do not require success or attribute the outcome to an attempt without support.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen for the names and pronouns used for the characters.
rows.think: Who do you mean by “she,” “he,” or “they”?
rows.clue: If the word could mean two people, use the name of the person you mean.
rows.moreHelp: Ask who a potentially unclear reference means. Contrast the possible referents already in the story and let the student choose; revise the reference without changing the event.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Listen to the two events. Can your listener tell when they happened?
rows.think: Did one happen first, or were they happening at the same time?
rows.clue: Try “after” if one came first, or “while” if they happened together.
rows.moreHelp: Use the learner’s two events. If they happened at the same time, model the link, as in “While Maya looked under the bench, Leo checked the swings.” Invite a retry using the learner’s own events.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen to the transition from what was happening to the problem.
rows.think: What was happening when the problem began?
rows.clue: If the problem interrupted something, try “Maya was ___ when ___.”
rows.moreHelp: Use the student’s two intended ideas to establish sequence, interruption, or contrast first. Offer connecting language for that relationship rather than a mixed list of unrelated connectors.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen to how the feeling connects with nearby story information.
rows.think: When did the character start feeling that way?
rows.clue: If it happened after an event, try “After ___, Maya felt ___.”
rows.moreHelp: Distinguish time from a reason for the feeling. Use a causal frame only if the student means that the event explains the feeling.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen to the plan and the idea you want to connect it with.
rows.think: Did the character make the plan before or after that event?
rows.clue: Use “before” or “after” if the listener needs help placing the plan in time.
rows.moreHelp: Clarify whether the student intends reason, purpose, or sequence. Choose a connector or clear reference for that relationship; do not require a feeling to cause every plan.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen to how the action connects with the surrounding events.
rows.think: Which action happened first?
rows.clue: Try “first” and “then” if the listener can’t tell the order from what you said.
rows.moreHelp: Have the student identify the actor and the event before or after the action. Repair unclear order or references; add a causal or purpose link only when intended.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen for how the object is introduced and referred to later.
rows.think: Which thing do you mean by “it” or “that”?
rows.clue: Name the object where the listener might be unsure.
rows.sentenceHelp: ___ found a ___. / The ___ / It ___ [when the reference is clear].
rows.moreHelp: Identify the intended object and each reference to it. Clarify the name or reference first; do not assume the character uses the object to solve the problem.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen to the link between the earlier events and the ending.
rows.think: Did the ending turn out the way the character expected?
rows.clue: If it turned out differently, try “Maya expected ___, but ___.”
rows.moreHelp: Establish the student’s intended relationship, then choose a time, result, or contrast structure. Do not treat finally as evidence of cause.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen for what may have caused the problem or what followed from it.
rows.think: What made the problem happen?
rows.clue: If one event caused the problem, try “The problem started because ___.”
rows.moreHelp: Choose one direction: reason for the problem or consequence of the problem. Identify the two supported ideas, then help express that causal link without reversing it.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen for the feeling and the information that may explain it.
rows.think: Why did the character feel that way?
rows.clue: Use a detail from your story that helps explain the feeling.
rows.moreHelp: Check the intended feeling and possible reason with the student. If the reason is unknown, permit uncertainty or decide to work on another supported causal relationship.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen for why the character chooses the plan.
rows.think: Why did the character choose that plan?
rows.clue: Tell what made that plan seem like a good choice to the character.
rows.moreHelp: Separate the problem, any relevant feeling or belief, and the intended plan. Have the student select the reason they mean; a feeling is not a required cause.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen for what the character does and what they intend to achieve.
rows.think: What happened because the character did that?
rows.clue: If the action made something change, tell what changed. If you’re explaining what the character hoped to do, say that instead.
rows.moreHelp: Contrast purpose and actual result using the student’s own story. Select one relationship for the current attempt; do not turn an intention into a successful consequence.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen for the object and any effect it has on what happens.
rows.think: Did using the object change what happened? How?
rows.clue: Tell what changed if it did. The object might help, make things harder, or make no difference.
rows.moreHelp: Establish whether the object is actually used or has another relevant effect. If no causal connection is supported, do not require one; select another meaningful causal target.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen for the outcome and what may have led to it.
rows.think: What made the ending turn out that way?
rows.clue: Use an event from your story that helps explain the ending. You can leave the reason open if the story doesn’t show it.
rows.moreHelp: Identify outcome and cause separately. Check direction with the student, then combine them; keep intended goals separate from actual results and allow an unresolved outcome.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen to what you have said about the character.
rows.think: What could you tell us about this character that would help us understand this part?
rows.clue: Try adding one detail about what the character did or what they were like.
rows.moreHelp: Ask what the listener still needs to understand about the character. Offer meaningful categories of detail, then have the student choose content that belongs in their story.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen to the place or time information already in your story.
rows.think: What could we see or hear in this place?
rows.clue: Add one detail that helps the listener picture where this happened.
rows.moreHelp: Identify what the listener cannot yet picture or understand. Invite one relevant place or time detail without requiring a causal explanation.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen to how you describe the problem.
rows.think: What would help us picture what went wrong?
rows.clue: Try telling exactly what got in the character’s way.
rows.sentenceHelp: The problem was ___. / ___ could not ___ because ___.
rows.moreHelp: Identify an information gap in the student’s account. Help choose a relevant detail; do not add escalation, obstacles, or stakes not intended by the student.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen to how the feeling is expressed.
rows.think: How could we tell how the character was feeling?
rows.clue: If your story gives a clue, add what the character said, did, or looked like.
rows.sentenceHelp: ___ felt ___. / ___ [an action or words expressing the feeling].
rows.moreHelp: Ask whether the student wants to name, explain, or show the feeling. Offer categories rather than inventing behavior; do not require both a feeling label and an explanation.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen to the plan you have expressed.
rows.think: What exactly was the character going to do?
rows.clue: Add one detail that makes the plan easier to picture, like where they meant to look.
rows.moreHelp: Identify what remains unclear about the intention. Have the student supply one needed detail and distinguish it from an action already completed.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen to the action you have described.
rows.think: How did the character do that?
rows.clue: Add one detail about how it happened, like what they used or where they looked.
rows.moreHelp: Choose one unclear part of the action with the student. Break it into meaningful components, then add the component the listener needs.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen to the information about the object.
rows.think: What about the object would help us picture it or understand how it was used?
rows.clue: Add one detail that matters here, like whether the bag was open or shut.
rows.moreHelp: Identify why the object is included in this story. Invite a description or actual use that supports that purpose; do not speculate about imaginary uses.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen to the outcome you have told.
rows.think: What was different at the end?
rows.clue: Add one detail about what changed or what stayed the same.
rows.moreHelp: Compare the ending with what the listener still needs to know. Help the student add one relevant outcome detail; do not require a new causal clause or moral.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen for information about what the character wants, thinks, feels, or knows.
rows.think: What does the character think, feel, or want here?
rows.clue: Use something the character said or did as a clue. You can say “might” if you aren’t sure.
rows.moreHelp: Identify a relevant internal state with the student and ask what supports it. Distinguish an explicit statement from an inference; allow uncertainty or more than one supported interpretation.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen for what the character notices or knows about the problem.
rows.think: What does the character know about the problem right now?
rows.clue: Tell what the character saw or heard. They might know less than the listener does.
rows.sentenceHelp: ___ knew ___. / ___ did not know ___. / ___ may have thought ___.
rows.moreHelp: Compare what is available to the character with what is available to the listener. Use a knowledge or belief statement only if the story supports that distinction.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen for the feeling and the surrounding story information.
rows.think: How might the character feel right here?
rows.clue: Look at what happened to this character. What in the story makes that feeling possible?
rows.moreHelp: Check whether the feeling is stated or inferred. Identify support with the student; do not replace their intended feeling or demand a single emotion when alternatives fit.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen for what the character wants or expects when making the plan.
rows.think: What does the character hope will happen?
rows.clue: Tell what they hoped for at that point, even if it turned out differently.
rows.moreHelp: Separate the intended goal or expectation from the actual outcome. Ask the student which internal state is supported and relevant; do not require the plan to come from a feeling.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen for the character’s action and any supported reason for choosing it.
rows.think: What might the character be trying to do here?
rows.clue: Use the action as a clue. If there are several possibilities, say “might.”
rows.sentenceHelp: ___ did ___ because they wanted ___. / ___ may have hoped ___.
rows.moreHelp: Check whether the motive is explicit or inferred. Identify supporting story information; if it is unknown, permit uncertainty rather than supplying a motive.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.

rows.lookListen: Look or listen for what the story shows about the character at the end.
rows.think: At the end, what does the character think, know, or feel?
rows.clue: Say what the story shows. Their thoughts or feelings can stay the same, change, or be unclear.
rows.sentenceHelp: At the end, ___ felt ___. / ___ still wanted ___. / ___ may have thought ___.
rows.moreHelp: Compare beginning and ending evidence only if a comparison serves the target. State a change in understanding only when supported; accept continuity or uncertainty and preserve the student’s interpretation.
rows.retry: Try this part again in your own words. Keep the meaning you intend; use less help if you can.
rows.reconnect: Tell this part with the relevant part before or after it, then return to the whole story.
